subject.title: Standardize async resource lifecycle management across retry/cleanup paths

question: Should OpenClaw add a shared async resource lifecycle/shutdown API across agent, gateway, and plugin cleanup paths, and which owner boundary should define it?
rationale: This issue is not a single broken code path; it would add or reshape lifecycle contracts across core runtime, plugin SDK/channel hooks, session state, and retry cleanup semantics.

options.title: Define a narrow shared lifecycle seam
options.body: Add a backward-compatible, owner-scoped drain/cancel API and prove it on one agent cleanup path plus one plugin or gateway path before broader migration.

options.title: Keep targeted lifecycle fixes
options.body: Continue fixing concrete races in their owning subsystems and close this design tracker once remaining symptoms are represented by narrower issues.

options.title: Defer until another concrete race
options.body: Leave current guards in place and revisit a shared API only when a new unfixed race shows existing hooks cannot express the needed cleanup ordering.

recommendation.title: Define a narrow shared lifecycle seam
recommendation.body: Add a backward-compatible, owner-scoped drain/cancel API and prove it on one agent cleanup path plus one plugin or gateway path before broader migration.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest sampled history across the session lifecycle, gateway, and outbound delivery paths this decision would cross.
